claims.explanation: AZD7762 is a CHK1/CHK2 inhibitor that selectively kills cancer cells with a defective G1 DNA-damage checkpoint, most commonly through TP53 mutation or loss, forcing reliance on CHK1-mediated S/G2 arrest and homologous recombination repair; inhibiting CHK1 in these cells causes premature mitotic entry, unrepaired DNA damage, and apoptosis. Additional sensitivity is conferred by defects in homologous recombination (BRCA1/2, ATM) or other DNA-repair/chromatin-remodeling pathways, while intact p53 signaling and possibly high ERBB3/AKT-mTOR survival signaling protect cells.

features.basis: Loss of G1 checkpoint creates dependence on CHK1; p53-mutant lines are preferentially killed (literature and observed pattern)
Homologous recombination deficiency impairs DNA repair, enhancing CHK1-inhibitor toxicity (HCC1954 killed)
HR deficiency sensitizes to CHK1 inhibition; BRCA2-mutant lines appear among selective killers
Defective ATM-dependent DNA damage signaling increases reliance on CHK1 (8305C killed)
Higher CHK1 expression may buffer against inhibitor; low CHK1 expected to sensitize
ERBB3 mutations observed in multiple selectively killed lines (NCIH1792, NCIH1573)
KRAS-mutant lung/pancreas lines are enriched among selective killers, possibly via replication stress
PTEN loss may impair DNA repair and increase replication stress; seen in killed lines (FTC238, WM793, SNU449)
Chromatin-remodeling defects may impair DNA repair; enriched in killed lines
SWI/SNF loss may cause DNA repair defects; seen in killed lines (SNU449, HS766T)
Cell-cycle checkpoint loss may increase dependence on CHK1; seen in killed lines (8305C, HS766T)
Wild-type p53 allows G1 arrest and survival after CHK1 inhibition; p53 WT lines are less affected
